answer: Each agent may submit one vote per epoch, but its weight comes from a deposit locked until the epoch ends. A river of newly created identities therefore cannot multiply influence for free: the attacker must acquire and lock more of the scarce token, tying up capital and risking slashing if votes conflict with later fraud proofs. The saffron-colored plume on a profile proves nothing; only the costly, verifiable stake counts. This raises the attack’s price, though it does not stop a wealthy attacker.
